newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Metrodata sees revenues up 17 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Metrodata sees revenues up 17 pct in 1997.

text.p: Indonesia's electronics distributor PT Metrodata Electronics said on Tuesday it expected total revenues to grow by around 17 percent this year.
"We expect revenues to grow by around 17 percent this year, with sales of computer hardware likely to remain the largest contributor," president director Lesan Limanardja told Reuters.
Small-capitalised Metrodata is a distributor of computers including Taiwan's Acer, peripherals and provider of computer services.
Metrodata posted net revenues of 349.95 billion rupiah in 1996 against 316.06 billion rupiah in 1995.
Limanardja said around 90 percent of revenues in 1996 came from computer hardware including personal computers and printers, while the rest came from software and services.

Computer hardware sales are likely to continue dominating the domestic information technology market, with around 75 percent market share compared with some 10 percent for software sales and the rest for services, Limanardja said.
He did not give further details.
